clue.text: Boat on page in blue artist's notebook

indicators.note: the boat-and-page pair sits inside the word for blue, which wraps round it

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A sad painter's sketchbook, bound in blue, has a little boat drawn on one of its pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of drawing paper is exactly the notebook an artist carries for rough drawings.

clue.text: Comment unfavourably on part of roof

definitions.meaning: to criticise harshly, as a critic pans a play
a thin grey stone tile laid on roofs

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs at a bit of the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to criticise severely; the noun is the split stone used for roofing tiles.

clue.text: Remove actor in crowd scene to join depleted cast

parts.note: a film extra is a non-speaking actor filling out a crowd

indicators.note: the word cast is emptied of its inner letters, leaving just its two ends

explanation.surface: A film director pulls one background actor out to bolster a cast that has lost members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted' strips cast down to its outside letters C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something out, as a dentist does a tooth, is a synonym for taking it away.

clue.text: Pursue legal proceedings involving hospital

indicators.note: the legal word takes the hospital letter into its middle

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit brought before a court
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone presses on with a lawsuit that concerns a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To go after someone or follow them hard is a straight synonym, as police do a suspect.

clue.text: Couple standing in picture concerned with male sexuality

indicators.note: the upturned couple goes inside the short word for a picture

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means set upright, so the word for couple is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A couple stand in a photo with a rather racy theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' signals the turnaround because this is a down clue, where the word is set upright.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Priapus, the Greek fertility god with an outsize phallus, the adjective relates to the penis or masculinity.

clue.text: Prospective partner harbouring grudge, ultimately leading to huge waste

indicators.note: the date holds the other pieces inside it like a harbour holding ships

parts.note: a date is someone you are going out with to see if a relationship develops

indicators.note: the grudge's last letter comes in front of the word for huge
only the final letter of grudge is wanted

parts.note: vast means huge

explanation.surface: A would-be partner nursing a grudge ends in a huge waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'huge' looks like part of the definition but supplies letters; the definition is 'waste' as a verb, as in lay waste.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay waste to a place is to ruin it utterly, the core sense of the verb.

clue.text: Sticky stuff for catching birds in tree

definitions.meaning: birdlime, a glue smeared on twigs to trap birds
the linden, a broad-leaved shade tree

explanation.surface: A bird-trapper smears glue in a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdlime is often shortened to the four-letter form, and the same word names the linden tree.

clue.text: Everyone held back by master, a 14th-century reformer

indicators.note: the word for master holds the turned-round word inside it

parts.note: a lord is a master, as in lord of the manor

indicators.note: back means the word for everyone is read the other way

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A medieval master restrains everyone, though one dissenting reformer stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA, which is 'held' by LORD.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of John Wycliffe in late medieval England were radical church reformers, forerunners of Protestantism.

clue.text: Villain's crimes upset social worker

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is just the noun villain

indicators.note: the letters of crimes are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: an ant is a worker in an insect colony, a social insect

explanation.surface: A villain's crimes have distressed the social worker assigned to the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' looks like a council employee, but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or scoundrel is the dictionary meaning; both words describe a criminal.

clue.text: Processed meat from old sheep given to setter

parts.note: past means former or old
a ram is a male sheep
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: Mutton from an elderly sheep is handed to the crossword setter, cured and processed.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoked, seasoned beef sliced thin for sandwiches is a cured, processed deli meat.

clue.text: Slave travelling round island with small bag

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the island letter
the letters of slave move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A slave journeys around an island carrying a little bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A small overnight suitcase or holdall is a classic synonym for a little travelling bag.

clue.text: Threat posed by fellow expert

parts.note: men are fellows; the clue gives the singular, a slip the blog and its commenters noted
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A colleague's skill poses a threat.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay needs MEN, but 'fellow' is singular, which gives MAN; the clue is faulty and most solvers write it in from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger or something threatening harm is the standard meaning of the noun.

clue.text: Soprano in Italian city runs over artist

indicators.note: the soprano letter goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Pisa, the Tuscan city of the Leaning Tower
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, doubled here for the plural
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An opera singer in Pisa runs over a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' must give two Rs, a stretch the blog's commenters queried. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Pissarro was a leading French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Correct relative inhaling cannabis

indicators.note: the relative takes the drug into its middle as a smoker draws in smoke

parts.note: a son is a relative
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A family member is caught smoking a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly right or accurate is the meaning of this informal British idiom.

clue.text: Food for trader

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
vender is a less common spelling of vendor, a seller

explanation.surface: Food set aside for a trader.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for food or fodder, especially animal feed or provisions.

clue.text: Unusual net domain chosen

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters of the two words gives a new word

explanation.surface: Someone has picked an odd internet domain name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put forward or selected for a role or award is what this past participle means.

clue.text: Ancient language in church (Latin) used by a senior cleric

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A dean conducts a church service in Latin, an ancient language.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are written in a different order from the clue: the L for Latin comes between A and DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aramaic language of ancient Babylonia was formerly called by this name.

clue.text: Container broken by mad macho driver

indicators.note: the container is split open with the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: a can is a container

indicators.note: the letters of macho go mad into a new order

explanation.surface: A crazed tough-guy motorist smashes a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but the definition is a horse-drawn carriage's driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drives a horse-drawn carriage was the driver of the era before motor cars.

clue.text: Fit in with conservative class

parts.note: a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A traditionalist settles in with the rest of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply or align with a rule or group is to fit in with it.

clue.text: Doctor Jones meeting old boy in surgery

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the name's letters are altered

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Doctor Jones meets a former pupil in his surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' poses as a title but rearranges JONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty is a cosmetic operation, an example of surgery.

clue.text: All one's possessions stored in highest ateliers

indicators.note: the letters are kept inside the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone's worldly goods are kept in the top-floor studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything a person owns, especially at death, is the legal sense of the word.

clue.text: City with great watering hole

parts.note: great can mean tall or large in stature
an inn is a pub, a watering hole

explanation.surface: A city boasting a fine pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital of Estonia on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Trees covering space by northern English hills

indicators.note: the trees surround the other pieces

parts.note: pines are trees
an en is a printing space, half an em

explanation.surface: Trees grow over the northern English hills.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printer's space, half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: The range of uplands running down northern England, called its backbone.

clue.text: Nasty relative listened to row

parts.note: ma is a mother, a relative

indicators.note: what is heard rather than read, so the word for row is taken by its sound

parts.note: a line is a row

explanation.surface: A nasty relative overheard an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means harmful or evil in intent, a synonym of nasty.

clue.text: Second tenor given central part of sketch in short piece of music

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: only the middle two letters of the word sketch are used

explanation.surface: A second tenor is given the middle part in a short comic sketch with music.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral composition for church use, often unaccompanied.

clue.text: Fellow leaving tree in swamp for wood

indicators.note: the fellow departs from the tree's name

parts.note: the mangrove grows in coastal swamps
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man leaves a swamp tree to look for timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wood or group of trees is the meaning, a synonym for copse.

clue.text: Clever head of Apple taking on Doctor of New Technology

indicators.note: only the first letter of apple is wanted

parts.note: o' is the shortened form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp
IT, information technology, the newer technology

explanation.surface: Apple's boss signs up a doctor of new technology.
explanation.walkthrough: The O comes from o', the clipped form of 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful and quick-witted, deft in handling things or situations.

clue.text: Get rid of judge with jumbled notes about it returned

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the turned-round pair
the letters of notes are mixed up
the word it is sent back the other way

explanation.surface: A judge jumbles his notes and hands back the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed pair sits inside the anagram, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw overboard or discard something no longer wanted.

clue.text: Piano tuner's first to leave punctually for concert

indicators.note: these letters go from the longer word

parts.note: prompt can mean exactly on time, as in at eight prompt
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: only the opening letter of tuner's is taken

explanation.surface: The piano tuner must leave on time for the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: PROMPT loses its second P and its T. A prom is a promenade concert, like the London Proms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Proms are a British summer season of classical concerts; a prom is one such event.

clue.text: Writer holding Underground up for one making her first appearance

indicators.note: the writer's name holds the reversed word

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, Italian poet

indicators.note: up reverses the word for Underground, though in an across clue it reads more naturally in a down

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground

explanation.surface: A writer is held up on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TUBE to EBUT, held by DANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman presented at her first social season makes her first appearance in society.
